data.title: bn-36x1: push-at-send delivers mentions into live push sessions from rite send

data.body: [HIGH] Mixed-version writers can erase claim ownership. src/core/claim.rs:33-39 adds owner as an optional field, so a pre-owner Rite binary ignores it and can append generic release or refresh events without owner. Current Rite then reads owner as absent while the live attachment remains. Failure modes: occupancy loss, ghost renewal, and duplicate responder spawn. Edge cases: an older installed binary, two checkouts with different versions, claims release --all, and old refresh followed by new renew. Rollback: do not depend on owner-bound claims until older writers are fenced, or use a representation they cannot mutate. Monitoring: detect owner-bound claim IDs followed by ownerless events and attached sessions without owned occupancy. Validation: create an owner-bound claim, run base-version release and refresh, then confirm current Rite rejects both mutations and preserves one holder.

[HIGH] Replacement is not crash-atomic, and routing observes both sessions. src/cli/sessions.rs:954-985 commits the successor before a separate predecessor detach. A crash, fsync error, or concurrent send can leave or observe both as attached. Reconciliation at src/cli/sessions.rs:366-430 never retires an attached predecessor named by a committed successor. push_deliveries at src/cli/sessions.rs:1452-1477 then sends one DM or mention to both. Failure modes: duplicate actions, private delivery to a superseded session, and permanent refusal of later attach. Edge cases: process death after commit, write failure during old detach, concurrent send in the window, and a later replace with two reservations. Rollback: disable replace, or make the committed replaces edge logically retire the predecessor before routing. Monitoring: flag multiple attached records per case-insensitive agent and multiple delivery results for one agent. Validation: stop after successor commit, restart, reconcile, and prove only the successor remains and receives one delivery.

[HIGH] Any adapter error is treated as proof that the harness died. src/cli/sessions.rs:1476-1486 detaches and releases agent occupancy after spawn errors, nonzero status, or the fixed timeout. The message body has no size bound and is copied into argv and RITE_BODY, so an addressed oversized message can make exec fail while the harness stays healthy. Transient queue errors have the same effect. Failure modes: a healthy session is evicted and a later message cold-spawns a duplicate responder. Edge cases: oversized bodies, busy queues, temporary PATH or daemon faults, one-body policy rejection, and concurrent sends. Rollback: retain attachment and claim on ambiguous delivery failure; detach only on SessionEnd or a trusted definitive session-not-found result. Monitoring: count failures by reason and alert on delivery failure followed by detach or hook spawn. Validation: keep a harness alive while one delivery fails or times out, send again, and assert no detach, release, or duplicate spawn; separately prove definitive session loss detaches.

[HIGH] A recipient-controlled adapter runs inside every sender context. src/core/session.rs:88-92 persists arbitrary deliver argv, and src/cli/sessions.rs:1516-1528 executes it without clearing inherited environment or setting a trusted working directory. Delivery also bypasses --no-hooks. A session registered from one project can therefore run code with another sender process environment, current directory, and inherited sandbox access when addressed. Failure modes: secret disclosure and writes through a cross-project confused deputy. Edge cases: shell adapters, relative executables, credential-bearing sender environments, and different workspace permission sets. Rollback: allow only trusted built-in adapters, or execute custom adapters through a fixed supervisor with a minimal environment and fixed directory. Monitoring: audit custom adapter registration and invocation with command identity and origin workspace. Validation: attach from a restricted workspace, send from a workspace with a unique secret and writable marker, and prove the adapter cannot read either.

[HIGH] The five-second timeout is not a process-tree or completion barrier. src/cli/sessions.rs:1535-1538 kills only the direct child, so descendants can survive and submit after Rite reports failure, detaches, and releases occupancy. Also, src/cli/sessions.rs:1545-1549 reads piped stderr only after the direct child exits; an inherited writer can keep that read blocked beyond five seconds. Failure modes: late duplicate delivery, orphan processes, and unbounded send latency. Edge cases: shell wrappers, background grandchildren, inherited stderr, and a descendant that submits after parent death. Rollback: run adapters in a process group, drain bounded stderr concurrently, and do not change occupancy until transport outcome is definitive. Monitoring: track adapter process groups, deadline overruns, surviving descendants, and late acknowledgments. Validation: use deterministic wrappers that retain stderr or submit after parent timeout, then assert bounded return, full tree termination, and no late delivery or occupancy release.

data.reason: BLOCK: five risk:high defects remain in mixed-version claim ownership, replacement atomicity, unverified failure detachment, sender-context custom adapter execution, and process-tree timeout handling. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains unsatisfied.
Resolved at 20c6da11: occupancy claims use a session attachment principal, and the sessions fold preserves owner across ownerless legacy records.
Resolved at 20c6da11: routing selects only the newest live attachment, and session reconciliation retires a committed successor predecessor.
Resolved at 20c6da11: ambiguous failures and oversized bodies keep occupancy; only explicit session-gone outcomes detach.

data.body: [HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The repair clears environment variables and changes cwd, but it does not isolate filesystem or process authority. src/core/session.rs:88-92 still persists arbitrary recipient-controlled argv. src/cli/sessions.rs:1646-1669 executes it with the sender process OS identity and inherited kernel sandbox. An absolute path or shell command can read or write every path allowed to the sender. Failure modes: secret disclosure, sender-workspace modification, and arbitrary command execution through a cross-project confused deputy. Edge cases: a human or agent sender with broader permissions, absolute paths, shell adapters, symlinks, HOME-readable credentials, and network access. Rollback: remove custom adapters from sender-side execution, or invoke a fixed broker under recipient-scoped least privilege. Monitoring: audit adapter provenance, executable identity, sender and recipient trust domains, and denied file or network access. Validation: register an adapter in a restricted workspace, address it from a context with a distinct readable secret and writable marker, and prove the adapter cannot access either by absolute path.

[HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The process group is killed only while the direct child remains alive. src/cli/sessions.rs:1697-1715 stops the deadline loop as soon as that child exits, then joins the stderr drain without a deadline. A wrapper can fork a descendant, exit 66, and leave the descendant running. If it keeps stderr open, join blocks indefinitely. If it closes stderr, it can submit later after Rite detached occupancy. Also, src/cli/sessions.rs:1752-1757 invokes an external kill command and ignores failure, after which child.wait can block forever. Failure modes: late duplicate delivery, orphan execution, false detach, and unbounded rite send latency. Edge cases: daemonizing wrappers, inherited stderr writers, quick exit 66, missing or shadowed kill, and kill permission failure. Rollback: use a checked OS killpg path, terminate and reap the group on every direct-child outcome, and bound stderr collection independently. Monitoring: record deadline overruns, drain-join duration, surviving process groups, kill failures, and late submissions. Validation: use deterministic wrappers whose leader exits while a child keeps stderr open or writes later, plus a forced kill failure; prove bounded return, no survivor, no late delivery, and no occupancy release before definitive completion.

[HIGH] Git sync can promote host-local session records into remote execution authority. src/sync/git.rs:392-396 merges origin/main wholesale, while .gitignore only affects untracked files. A tracked local/sessions.jsonl from an older store, another machine, or a compromised remote survives the merge. src/cli/sessions.rs:1505-1568 then trusts that record and runs its arbitrary deliver argv. The push path at src/sync/git.rs:297-324 also pushes the whole branch without the claimed path exclusion. Failure modes: session-id disclosure, cross-host routing takeover, and arbitrary adapter execution in a sender context. Edge cases: previously tracked local files, old stores without the ignore rule, manual commits, malicious remote commits, and pull before any local sync commit. Rollback: reject or remove local/** from both outgoing and incoming trees, migrate existing repositories, and fail closed before delivery when session state is Git-tracked or remote-derived. Monitoring: make doctor and sync status alert on tracked local/** paths and reject pulls or pushes containing them. Validation: commit a crafted local/sessions.jsonl on a remote, pull it into a clean host, and prove Rite rejects or quarantines it and never executes its adapter; also prove an existing tracked local file cannot be pushed.

data.reason: BLOCK: three risk:high defects remain. Custom adapters still inherit sender filesystem authority; exited leaders can leave descendants or hang stderr collection; Git sync can import tracked host-local session records and execute their adapter commands. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains unsatisfied.

Resolved at d4d8ce: session records now carry only an adapter name. The sending host supplies argv from local configuration or the builtin table. Unknown names do not run, so a recipient no longer supplies arbitrary sender-side argv.

data.body: [HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The latest cleanup still cannot contain descendants that leave the original process group. src/cli/sessions.rs:1683-1697 treats ESRCH as proof that the group is dead. A descendant can call setsid before its leader exits 66. The later kill targets only the old PGID. src/cli/sessions.rs:1808 bounds stderr collection, but the escaped process can still act. Rite then classifies the result as SessionGone at src/cli/sessions.rs:1834-1837 and detaches. Also, a timeout followed by killpg failure reaches the unbounded child.wait at src/cli/sessions.rs:1801-1805. Failure modes: late delivery, orphan execution, false detach, and unbounded send latency. Edge cases: daemonizing adapters, setsid, retained stderr, and kill permission failure. Rollback: use a non-escaping supervisor or cgroup, and keep occupancy on uncertain cleanup. Monitoring: record escaped descendants, kill errors, drain timeouts, and late submissions. Validation: use deterministic setsid wrappers and forced kill failures. Prove bounded return, no survivors, no late action, and no detach without definitive completion.

[HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The tracked-path guard has a check-to-use race with pull. src/cli/sessions.rs:1538-1568 loads sessions, checks the index, and then loads the adapter table in separate operations. src/sync/git.rs:400-434 merges remote local state before quarantine. A concurrent push can observe a clean index, then load a remote local/adapters.json after merge. A remote entry can override the builtin codex adapter and execute its argv. Pull can also replace or remove valid host-local state before quarantine. Failure modes: remote command execution, session loss, and cross-host routing. Edge cases: an absent local adapter file, a remote codex override, ignored local files, and concurrent send during pull. Rollback: quarantine the fetched tree before merging, or serialize pull and delivery with one lock. Monitoring: log adapter-table identity, pull overlap, rejected remote local paths, and local-state replacement. Validation: pause send after the clean check, pull a crafted adapter, then resume. Prove no command runs and the original host state remains.

[HIGH] Push checks only the tip tree for host-local state. src/sync/git.rs:307-313 accepts a clean HEAD, then src/sync/git.rs:328-331 pushes the full reachable branch. src/sync/git.rs:234-274 can create a deletion commit after an older commit captured local sessions or adapters. The clean tip therefore passes while Git still transfers the sensitive historical blobs. Failure modes: disclosure of session identifiers, adapter commands, embedded secrets, and later resurrection from remote history. Edge cases: pre-ignore stores, manual force-add, an add-then-delete branch, and an upstream behind both commits. Rollback: reject any outgoing commit range containing local paths, or rewrite that data from history before push. Monitoring: scan every outbound tree and remote ref for local paths. Validation: create one local-data commit and one deletion commit, then invoke rite sync push to a bare remote. Prove Rite refuses or the remote lacks every local blob and path.

data.reason: BLOCK: three risk:high defects remain. Escaped adapter descendants can survive or hang cleanup. A concurrent pull can pass the tracked-state check and supply executable adapter configuration. A clean tip can still push sensitive local state from reachable history. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains unsatisfied.

data.body: [HIGH][UNRESOLVED] Stderr EOF still does not prove that every adapter descendant stopped. src/cli/sessions.rs:1692-1702 kills only the original process group. src/cli/sessions.rs:1821-1827 treats pipe EOF as cleanup evidence, and src/cli/sessions.rs:1865-1868 then accepts exit 66 as SessionGone. A child can call setsid, close stderr, and continue after its leader exits 66. The old group returns ESRCH, EOF arrives, Rite detaches occupancy, and the escaped child can submit later. Failure modes: false detach, late duplicate delivery, orphan execution, and responder overlap. Edge cases: setsid with stderr redirected to /dev/null, double-fork daemonization, inherited descriptors closed before work, and quick leader exit. Rollback: never detach from an adapter result unless a non-escaping supervisor proves full-tree completion, or keep occupancy for every result that cannot provide that proof. Monitoring: record adapter supervisor identity, surviving descendants, late submissions, and detach-followed-by-delivery. Validation: use deterministic barriers with a setsid child that closes stderr, exits the leader with 66, then writes or submits later. Prove the child cannot survive and occupancy remains unless cleanup is definitive.

[HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The outgoing-history scan can omit reachable sensitive commits and can inspect a different ref than the one pushed. src/sync/git.rs:490-505 uses path-limited git log with default history simplification against HEAD. A merged side branch can add and delete local state, produce a TREESAME merge, and be pruned from this path history while its commits remain reachable. Also, src/sync/git.rs:338-341 pushes main even when HEAD names another branch. Failure modes: disclosure of session identifiers, adapter commands, embedded secrets, and later resurrection from remote history. Edge cases: add-delete side branches, TREESAME merges, non-main checkouts, detached HEAD, missing origin/main, and git-log errors that currently return an empty list. Rollback: inspect the exact main ref that will be pushed, enumerate every reachable outgoing commit without history simplification, and fail closed on inspection errors. Monitoring: audit pushed object ranges for local paths and compare the scanned OID with the pushed OID. Validation: create a merged side branch that adds then deletes local/sessions.jsonl, and repeat from a non-main checkout. Prove rite sync push refuses both and the bare remote receives no sensitive blob.

[HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The pre-merge guard still has a mutable-ref race with pull and delivery. src/sync/git.rs:410-425 checks origin/main and later merges that ref by name. A second pull can fetch a new malicious origin/main after the first check but before its merge. The first pull then merges unchecked local state. Concurrent send also checks the index before reading adapters in separate operations at src/cli/sessions.rs:1542-1572, so it can load the imported adapter during that window. Failure modes: remote command execution, host-local session replacement, session loss, and cross-host routing takeover. Edge cases: two concurrent pulls, a force-updated remote, an absent local adapter file, a remote codex override, and send paused after its clean-index check. Rollback: resolve and verify one immutable fetched commit, merge that exact OID, and serialize pull plus session and adapter reads under one data-directory lock. Monitoring: log checked and merged OIDs, pull overlap, adapter-table identity, and rejected remote local paths. Validation: use deterministic barriers so one pull changes origin/main after the other checks it, then resume a paused send. Prove the unchecked commit never merges, no remote adapter runs, and original local state remains.

data.reason: BLOCK: three risk:high defects remain. Escaped adapter descendants can close stderr and survive a false SessionGone detach. The outgoing scan can miss TREESAME side-branch history or inspect HEAD while main is pushed. Pull checks mutable origin/main before merging it, leaving a concurrent remote-adapter execution race. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains unsatisfied.
Resolved at 9ab1358b: adapter outcomes only report session_gone and keep the attachment and claim. Escaped descendants can no longer trigger false occupancy release.
Resolved at 9ab1358b for the reported exact-case history and ref defect: push scans every outgoing main commit tree without history simplification and fails closed on scan errors.

data.body: [HIGH][UNRESOLVED] The local-state boundary remains case-sensitive although macOS is supported. src/sync/git.rs:490-501 and src/sync/git.rs:565-575 query only the exact pathspec local, while src/sync/git.rs:430-442 accepts and merges when that query is empty. On a case-insensitive macOS volume, a remote tree containing LOCAL/sessions.jsonl and LOCAL/adapters.json aliases the runtime paths at src/core/project.rs:172-185; push_deliveries then reads them and executes configured argv through src/cli/sessions.rs:1542-1573 and src/cli/sessions.rs:1724-1751. A read-only Git check confirmed that core.ignoreCase=true does not make these tree or index pathspecs match wrong-case paths. Failure modes: remote command execution, session takeover, and host data exposure. Edge cases: LOCAL, Local, mixed-case nested paths, and default macOS volumes. Rollback: enumerate every tree and index path, then reject a case-folded first component equal to local before merge, push, or delivery. Monitoring: report tracked case-fold aliases and adapter provenance. Validation: on macos-latest, pull a remote with uppercase crafted records and assert rejection and no adapter execution; repeat the outgoing scan.

data.reason: BLOCK: one risk:high defect remains. Case-variant local paths bypass sync and delivery guards on supported case-insensitive macOS filesystems, allowing a crafted sync remote to supply executable session adapter state. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains unsatisfied.

data.body: [HIGH][RESOLVED] Commit 8451239a closes the case-variant host-local-state bypass. src/sync/git.rs:493-503 case-folds the first component after listing complete trees and the index; src/sync/git.rs:529-575 applies it to every outgoing main commit; src/sync/git.rs:417-445 checks and merges one immutable remote commit; src/cli/sessions.rs:1566-1573 refuses delivery when any case variant is tracked. Failure modes reviewed: remote adapter execution, session takeover, and host-data exposure. Edge cases reviewed: LOCAL, Local, mixed-case first components, outgoing side-branch history, non-main checkout, and inspection failure. Rollback: disable sync push and pull, then revert this repair if the guards regress. Monitoring: report tracked case-fold aliases, checked and merged OIDs, and adapter provenance. Validation: static tracing covers incoming, outgoing, quarantine, index, and delivery paths; focused tests cover uppercase pull, push, and tracked-host rejection. No residual defect remains in this thread.

data.reason: Resolved at 8451239a: all tree and index guards enumerate paths and reject a case-insensitive first component equal to local.

LGTM for the full persisted range through 8451239a. The case-fold repair closes the final HIGH sync-to-local execution path. Best-effort duplicate delivery, host-owned adapters, advisory claims, and the documented concurrent sync limitation remain explicit boundaries. This source vote does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.
